structuredContent.body:
Poll keys containing lone UTF-16 surrogate units can evade SQLite deduplication and start another run on every poll. This change rejects those derived identities before lookup or admission, with bounded typed diagnostics. Item mode isolates malformed candidates while preserving whole-batch type, blank, length and valid-duplicate errors; single mode validates the existing 512-unit slice. Valid pairs, literal U+FFFD and intentional no-key behavior retain their exact semantics.

Closes #361. Closes #483.

The #483 prerequisite adds the established optional garbage-collection step to two Windows SQLite test cleanup hooks. Its pre-existing failure reproduced on unchanged main. Product assertions, timeouts, retries and coverage thresholds are unchanged. ADR-0079 and the trigger documentation describe the identity rule; historical stored data is not rewritten.

Validation on source candidate `420240cad27d3865988dc7009dc9d80291e93c9c`:

- API coverage: 1,943 passed, 14 documented skips; 95.95% lines and 90.88% branches, using two local workers. Domain: 460 tests, 98.73% lines and 96.09% branches. Typecheck, affected lint/format and seven forced API build tasks passed.
- Independent QA: 21 native scheduler/HTTP/SQLite observations across same-file restart, 15 exact durable IDs with matching queued events, held-response overlap checks, 20 controlled public-method cases, and one-process concurrent file-SQLite admission. Disposable stores and owned processes were cleaned up.
- The native supervisor's original exit 1 is retained: two warning timestamps preceded the separate probe clock by 1 ms. Offline analysis of the unchanged logs used recorded gateway due times and assigned all 20 warnings uniquely. The native sequence was not rerun.
- Original coverage, cleanup and baseline failures remain published. The genuine build ran before the source commit; all twelve changed source files and the complete compiled inventories were rebound to the committed bytes.

Evidence: [baseline](docs/qa/2026-11-15-poll-dedupe-baseline/README.md), [implementation and cleanup diagnosis](docs/qa/2026-11-15-poll-dedupe-implementation/README.md), [independent corrected QA](docs/qa/2026-11-15-poll-dedupe-corrected/README.md). This publication also retains the preceding Space cards [final completion](docs/qa/2026-11-15-space-cards-completion/README.md) and [corrected CI](docs/qa/2026-11-15-space-cards-corrected-ci/README.md), without changing that product source or its pending owner acceptance.

Delivery gates: independent Claude Opus 5.5 xhigh review, current-head CI and fresh GPT-6 Astra max exact-head/target sign-off remain pending. Three formal scans maximum, shared by the opposite-family review and final audit. QA agent: `/root/runtime_361_qa` (GPT-6.1 Sol xhigh). Human QA is not required for these two issues. Other batch acceptance obligations remain open.

Found by the independent Claude Opus 5.5 review of WP-C3 (#140 investigation) on 2026-10-19, through the public API against the built binary with real SQLite. Outside every I01 to I07 bolt; filed for triage.

## Defect

A poll candidate whose dedupe key contains a lone UTF-16 surrogate is never recognised as already admitted, so it starts a new run on every poll, without bound.

## Steps

1. Publish a loop with a poll trigger: `intervalSeconds: 5`, an http probe to a loopback source, `fireWhen: 'true'`, `items: { select: 'probe.json', dedupeKey: 'item.key', maxRunsPerPoll: 5 }`, then an input wait and an exit.
2. Let the source return `[{"key":"lone-\ud800-key"},{"key":"sg-a"},{"key":"sg-b"}]` with the `\ud800` sent as a JSON escape.
3. Observe three polls.

Expected: the lone-surrogate key is admitted once (or refused once with a typed diagnostic); `sg-a` and `sg-b` are admitted once each.

Actual: a new run for the lone-surrogate key on every poll (three polls gave three runs); `sg-a` and `sg-b` were admitted once each.

## Cause (confirmed in-process)

libsql binds the key parameter as U+FFFD (`EF BF BD`), while `json_extract` decodes the stored `\ud800` escape as `ED A0 80`, so `findTriggerDedupeKeys` and the in-transaction key check never match. `hasTriggerDedupe` (single-result polls) most likely has the same problem; not verified.

## Where

`packages/domain/src/poll-items.ts` (candidate key validation) and the SQLite dedupe lookups in `packages/infrastructure/src/sqlite`. Options: refuse keys that are not well-formed UTF-16 with a typed per-candidate diagnostic (consistent with D-020 in `docs/delivery/2026-10-18-i01-i07-register.md`), or normalise keys before storing and comparing.

## Related

#140 (poll starvation; the structural-depth refusal landed there), UoW #300 admission boundary.

issue.title: Release closed SQLite fixture handles before Ollama test cleanup on Windows
issue.body:
Verification prerequisite discovered during #361 in the authorized four-intent delivery batch.

## Reproduction and scope

The unchanged `apps/api/src/ollama-container.test.ts` and `apps/api/src/preflight-ollama.test.ts` cleanup hooks fail with Windows `EBUSY` deleting disposable SQLite database or sidecar files after their clients close. The failures occurred in the first candidate API coverage run and a one-worker four-file isolation run. A separate one-worker baseline run at `e1237593babd4d03466b91685fc05dbe49223b2a` (tree identical to merged main `15ce9a1dd12e87b7f7cb5f853aaecf68d6188afd`) reproduced four cleanup failures with 21 passing tests. Baseline and candidate matched 123 relevant raw source/config/lockfile blobs and seven installed dependency files, including the native libsql binary. Node was 22.23.4. This is pre-existing test teardown behavior, not a poll regression.

The existing `ollama-startup.test.ts` and API subprocess helper already collect closed native statements before removing SQLite fixtures. `docs/research/sqlite-libsql.md` documents this Windows behavior. The two failing hooks omit that collection step.

## Accepted bounded correction

Apply the established `globalThis.gc?.()` cleanup step after fixture shutdown/reference and mock cleanup, before `rm`, in these two test hooks only. Preserve all product code, assertions, timeouts, retry configuration and coverage floors. Cleanup must still fail if removal fails. No broad temp deletion or process termination.

## Acceptance and delivery

- Retain original coverage, isolated-candidate and unchanged-baseline failures.
- Both affected specs pass with the same one-worker invocation after the narrow correction.
- Full API coverage passes with unchanged thresholds; report any reduced local worker count explicitly.
- Current-head CI, independent Claude review, independent QA and final Astra gate cover this prerequisite alongside the #361 patch.

Implementation: GPT-6 Luna xhigh. Opposite-family review: Claude Opus 5.5 xhigh. QA: the #361 independent delivery worker and current CI. This issue carries no owner-only acceptance obligation.

Duplicate search covered existing issues for `EBUSY` and Ollama cleanup; no matching root cause was found. Evidence is published with [PR #484](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/pull/484).

## Delivery progress — 2026-11-15

The exact two-hook correction is included in source `420240cad27d3865988dc7009dc9d80291e93c9c` and publication head `08651317c485062eb90367e1df3f7632f8e1a6c7`. The first corrected one-worker pair passed 25/25 tests; the subsequent full API coverage run passed 1,943 tests with 14 documented skips at 95.95% lines and 90.88% branches using two workers. Original candidate, isolation and unchanged-main cleanup failures remain retained in the [implementation evidence](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/blob/08651317c485062eb90367e1df3f7632f8e1a6c7/docs/qa/2026-11-15-poll-dedupe-implementation/README.md).

QA roles: `/root/runtime_361_impl` (GPT-6.1 Sol xhigh) performed the complete API gate independently of the Luna-authored cleanup change; `/root/runtime_361_qa` (GPT-6.1 Sol xhigh) performed the separate #361 behavior verification. Current-head CI, Claude Opus 5.5 xhigh review and fresh Astra max sign-off remain pending on PR #484. No merge or closure is claimed.
